name: Piper PA-23 Apache / Aztec
variants: Aztec / Aztec A–F (swept square fin, long nose)
summary: Piper's first twin: the early Apache and the larger, longer-nosed Aztec, a sturdy six-seat utility and freight twin.

wings: Low, thick constant-chord wing with squared tips
Engines mounted close to the fuselage
engines: Two flat engines in squat nacelles; short and rounded on the early version
fuselage: Aztec has a long nose with baggage compartment; Apache nose is short and rounded
tail: Aztec: tall swept fin with a square top and all-moving stabilator

tellTales: Boxy, slab-sided cabin on a low-wing piston twin
Thick constant-chord wing with squared tips
Tall, square-cornered swept fin (rounded fin on the earlier version)

confusedWith.howToTell: The 310 has wingtip fuel tanks and a sleeker fuselage; the Aztec is boxier with plain wingtips.
The Baron has a tapered wing and a sleek rounded fuselage; the Aztec has a thick constant-chord wing and slab sides.
The Seneca has a tapered wing and a slimmer six-window cabin; the Aztec has a thick rectangular wing and a boxier fuselage.
The Twin Comanche is slimmer and sleeker with a sloping nose and a raked fin; the Apache/Aztec is boxier with a thick wing.
